recalls.vin.s2b: Use their recall lookup, or call

drone.title: Drone pilot path
drone.subtitle: Rules, certificate and fees · Transport Canada
drone.loading: Checking Transport Canada’s rules and fees…
drone.error.title: We couldn’t build your drone plan
drone.error.body: Transport Canada’s page explains each category of operation and the certificate it needs.
drone.handoff.portalNote: In Transport Canada’s Drone Management Portal, you register your drone, take the exam, get your certificate and pay the fees.
drone.handoff.specialNote: Apply for a Special Flight Operations Certificate before you fly.
drone.handoff.microNote: On tc.canada.ca. No registration or certificate, but safety rules still apply.
drone.fines: Fines for individuals go up to $1,000 for flying without a certificate and $5,000 for an unregistered or unmarked drone.
drone.verdict.micro.sub: Drones under 250 g are microdrones. You still have to fly safely and respect other people’s privacy.
drone.verdict.basic: You need a Basic pilot certificate
drone.verdict.basic.sub: One online exam, and you’re certified the moment you pass. Register your drone first.
drone.verdict.advanced: You need an Advanced pilot certificate
drone.verdict.advanced.sub: Pass the Advanced Exam and an in-person flight review, and fly a drone declared safe for what you’ll do.
drone.verdict.complex: You need a Level 1 Complex certificate
drone.verdict.complex.sub: For lower-risk flights beyond visual line-of-sight, in uncontrolled airspace below 122 m (400 ft), under an RPAS Operator Certificate.
drone.verdict.special: You need Transport Canada’s permission first
drone.verdict.special.sub: Advertised events and drones over 150 kg need a Special Flight Operations Certificate (SFOC-RPAS).
drone.size.title: How heavy is your drone?
drone.size.note: Weight includes anything attached, like a camera or guards, but not the remote control.
drone.op.title: How will you fly?
drone.op.standard.sub: More than 30 m from bystanders, in uncontrolled airspace, where you can see it
drone.op.near-people.sub: Within 30 m of bystanders (horizontally), or over them
drone.op.controlled-airspace: Near an airport or in controlled airspace
drone.op.controlled-airspace.sub: Within 5.6 km of a certified airport, 1.9 km of a heliport, or with air traffic control permission
drone.op.bvlos.sub: Out of your sight, for example inspections or surveying
drone.op.event.sub: A concert, festival, market or sporting event, any size of drone
drone.op.microHint: For a microdrone, only an advertised event changes the answer.
drone.young.title: Or fly a microdrone on your own.
drone.young.micro: Drones under 250 g need no certificate or registration, at any age.
drone.young.owner: A drone of 250 g or more must be registered by an owner who is 14 or older.
drone.steps.title: Your path, step by step
drone.step.register.detail: Takes about 3 minutes online. Mark the registration number on the drone.
drone.step.exam-basic.detail: Online, 35 questions in 90 minutes, 65% to pass. You can retry after 24 hours. Minimum age 14.
drone.step.exam-advanced.detail: Online, 50 questions in 60 minutes, 80% to pass. Keep your reference number. Minimum age 16.
drone.step.ground-school.detail: At a drone flight school. Minimum age 18 for Level 1 Complex.
drone.step.review.detail: In person with a Transport Canada-approved reviewer at a flight school. Bring your exam results, government ID and drone registration.
drone.step.cert-basic.detail: Issued right after you pass. Download and print it from the portal.
drone.step.cert-advanced.detail: Issued as soon as you pay in the Drone Management Portal.
drone.step.cert-complex: Apply for your Level 1 Complex certificate
drone.step.cert-complex.detail: Issued as soon as you pay in the Drone Management Portal.
drone.step.rpoc: Fly under an RPAS Operator Certificate
drone.step.rpoc.detail: Required for beyond visual line-of-sight flights: you, your company or your employer declares the right procedures are in place.
drone.step.declaration: Use a drone declared for the job
drone.step.declaration.detail: Most advanced operations need a drone with a safety assurance declaration for that operation. Check the manufacturer’s declaration.
drone.step.fly.detail: Carry your certificate and registration. Your certificate doesn’t expire, but you need a recency activity every 24 months.
drone.feeNote: Transport Canada fees total {total} on {date}. They rise slightly every April 1. Schools and reviewers set their own prices.
drone.micro.1: Don’t fly in a way that could put aircraft or people at risk.
drone.micro.2: Stay away from emergency sites like fires, crashes and floods.
drone.micro.3: Transport Canada recommends keeping it in sight, below 122 m (400 ft), and far from airports and heliports.
drone.micro.4: Flying at an advertised event, even a microdrone, needs a Special Flight Operations Certificate.
drone.special.1: Apply for a Special Flight Operations Certificate (SFOC-RPAS) before the flight.
drone.special.2: A fee applies, based on how complex the operation is. Government emergency responders are exempt.
drone.special.3: The page explains what to include in your application.
drone.special.link: Get permission for special drone operations
boat.title: Boating: who can drive?
boat.subtitle: Pleasure Craft Operator Card · Transport Canada
boat.error.title: We couldn’t check the boating rules
boat.error.body: Transport Canada’s page explains who needs proof of competency and the limits for young operators.
boat.handoffNote: Courses and tests are online or in class. Providers set the fees; none go to the government.
boat.verdict.ok: {who, select, you {{kind, select, pwc {Yes, you can drive this personal watercraft} other {Yes, you can drive this boat}}} other {{kind, select, pwc {Yes, {an, select, yes {an} other {a}} {age}-year-old can drive this personal watercraft} other {Yes, {an, select, yes {an} other {a}} {age}-year-old can drive this boat}}}}
boat.verdict.ok.sub: With proof of competency on board, usually the Pleasure Craft Operator Card. Any motor counts, even an electric trolling motor that’s turned off.
boat.verdict.no-motor: No card needed without a motor
boat.verdict.no-motor.sub: Proof of competency only applies to boats fitted with a motor. A sailboat with an auxiliary motor needs it, even under sail.
boat.verdict.north: No proof of competency needed in Nunavut or the NWT
boat.verdict.north.sub: The operator card and the youth horsepower limits don’t apply in those waters. Taking a course is still a good idea.
boat.verdict.supervised: Only with someone 16 or older in the boat
boat.verdict.supervised.sub: Alone, {an, select, yes {an} other {a}} {age}-year-old can drive up to {limit} hp. With direct supervision they can drive more, with their own proof of competency.
boat.verdict.pwc-under16: No: under 16 can’t drive a personal watercraft
boat.verdict.pwc-under16.sub: Not even with an adult on board. Sea-Doos, jet skis and other PWCs are 16 and older only.
boat.supervised: Someone 16+ is in the boat, supervising
boat.supervised.sub: “Direct supervision” means they’re on board and watching the driver
boat.north: Boating in Nunavut or the NWT
boat.rules.title: Limits for young drivers
boat.rules.u12.body: Up to 10 hp (7.5 kW) without direct supervision.
boat.rules.u16.body: Up to 40 hp (30 kW) without direct supervision.
boat.rules.pwc.body: No personal watercraft, even with supervision.
boat.rules.note: These limits don’t apply in Nunavut or the Northwest Territories. Visitors using their own boat in Canada for less than 45 days in a row don’t need Canadian proof of competency.
boat.rules.visitors: Visitors using their own boat in Canada for less than 45 days in a row don’t need Canadian proof of competency.
boat.rules.north: These limits don’t apply in Nunavut or the Northwest Territories.
boat.get.title: How to get your card
boat.get.1.body: Only providers accredited by Transport Canada can test you and issue the card. Courses are online or in a classroom.
boat.get.2.body: Usually at the end of the course. You can skip the course and write the test in person under supervision. Didn’t pass? Try again after 24 hours.
boat.get.3.body: It’s valid for life. A paper or electronic copy isn’t accepted: carry the card itself.
boat.other.1: Renting? A completed rental boat safety checklist counts as proof of competency for the rental period.
boat.other.2: Lost your card? Your course provider can replace it for a fee. Transport Canada’s lookup finds your provider.
travel.subtitle: Within Canada or across the border
travel.error.title: We couldn’t load the travel rules
travel.error.body: The official page explains what you can bring.
travel.cannabis.title: Travelling with cannabis
travel.cannabis.domestic-flight.sub: In your carry-on or checked bag, within the 30 g public possession limit.
travel.cannabis.domestic-flight.1: Adults can carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis in public, or the equivalent in other forms.
travel.cannabis.domestic-flight.2: Oils, drinks and other liquid or topical forms go in your 1 L clear bag with your other liquids in carry-on.
travel.cannabis.domestic-flight.3: You’re responsible for knowing the laws where you land: each province and territory has its own rules.
travel.cannabis.domestic-road: Yes, within the 30 g public limit
travel.cannabis.domestic-road.sub: Adults can carry legal cannabis within Canada, up to the 30 g public possession limit.
travel.cannabis.domestic-road.1: Adults can carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis in public, or the equivalent in other forms.
travel.cannabis.domestic-road.2: You’re responsible for the laws of the province or territory you’re in, and they differ. Check before you go.
travel.cannabis.domestic-road.3: Route passes through the U.S.? Leave it behind: crossing the border with cannabis is illegal.
travel.cannabis.entering-canada.sub: Bringing cannabis into Canada in any form or amount is a serious criminal offence, even from places where it’s legal.
travel.cannabis.entering-canada.1: This includes edibles, extracts, topicals and CBD products.
travel.cannabis.entering-canada.2: If you have any with you, you must declare it to the CBSA. Not declaring can bring arrest, prosecution and penalties up to $2,000.
travel.cannabis.entering-canada.3: A penalty can also get your NEXUS or FAST membership refused or cancelled.
travel.cannabis.leaving-canada.sub: Taking cannabis out of Canada in any form or amount is illegal, even to places where it’s legal.
travel.cannabis.leaving-canada.1: This includes edibles, extracts, topicals and CBD products.
travel.cannabis.leaving-canada.2: Abroad, including in the U.S., you could be charged and refused entry in the future.
travel.cannabis.leaving-canada.3: Flying out of Canada with cannabis is illegal: leave it at home before you head to the airport.
travel.cannabis.medical.title: Medical cannabis too.
travel.cannabis.medical.body: A medical document isn’t a permit to cross the border. Only Health Canada can authorize it, in rare cases, and every country on your route must allow it.
travel.cannabis.handoffOkNote: What you can bring on a plane: the Canadian Air Transport Security Authority’s screening rules for cannabis.
travel.cannabis.handoffNoNote: Cannabis at the border, from the Canada Border Services Agency.
travel.cannabis.handoffRoadNote: Health Canada’s page on the 30 g public limit and what counts toward it.
travel.calc.title: How much can you carry?
travel.calc.max.g: Most you can carry of this alone: {max} g
travel.calc.max.seeds: Most you can carry of this alone: {max} seeds
travel.calc.note: Health Canada equivalents: 1 g dried = 5 g fresh = 15 g of solids = 70 g of non-solids (like lotions) = 0.25 g of concentrates = 570 g of beverages = 1 seed. Adults only, for non-medical use.
travel.pets.title: Travelling with a pet
travel.pets.entering.sub: Dogs and cats 3 months or older, coming from most countries including the U.S., need proof of a current rabies vaccination to enter or return to Canada.
travel.pets.entering.1: The certificate must be in English or French, signed by a licensed veterinarian, identify your {pet} and show the vaccination is current.
travel.pets.entering.2: Other rules can apply depending on where you’re coming from, your {pet}’s age and whether it travels with you. Check CFIA’s tool before you book.
travel.pets.entering.3: If your {pet} doesn’t meet the rules at the border, it may be ordered removed from Canada, and you could face fines.
travel.pets.entering-young: Under 3 months: no rabies certificate needed
travel.pets.entering-young.sub: Puppies and kittens under 3 months don’t need a rabies vaccination certificate to enter Canada, but other rules can apply.
travel.pets.entering-young.1: Check CFIA’s import tool for your situation: it depends on the country you’re coming from and why your {pet} is coming.
travel.pets.entering-young.2: Bringing in an animal to sell, adopt out, foster or breed? Commercial imports follow different rules.
travel.pets.entering-young.3: Your airline may ask for more, like a health certificate or a specific carrier.
travel.pets.entering-other: Check CFIA’s rules for your animal
travel.pets.entering-other.sub: For CFIA, only dogs, cats and ferrets count as pets. Birds, rabbits, reptiles and others have their own import rules.
travel.pets.entering-other.1: Look up your animal in CFIA’s import tool before you travel: some need permits or health certificates.
travel.pets.entering-other.2: Some requirements must be done within set timeframes, so start early.
travel.pets.entering-other.3: Your airline may also have its own rules for your animal.
travel.pets.leaving-canada.sub: Each country sets its own requirements for pets, and they change often. Start with your veterinarian as soon as you know your dates.
travel.pets.leaving-canada.1: Most countries need an export certificate from a licensed vet, endorsed by a CFIA veterinarian.
travel.pets.leaving-canada.2: To come home, your {pet} must still meet Canada’s import rules, like a valid rabies certificate.
travel.pets.leaving-canada.3: Keep printed and digital copies of every document.
travel.pets.domestic-flight.sub: Call your airline well before you fly: they decide whether your {pet} rides in the cabin or the hold, and what carrier and papers you need.
travel.pets.domestic-flight.1: At security, take your {pet} out of the carrier, send the carrier through the scanner and carry your pet through the metal detector.
travel.pets.domestic-flight.2: Don’t hand your {pet} to a screening officer or put it on the conveyor belt.
travel.pets.domestic-flight.3: The carrier should let your {pet} lie down, turn around and stand up comfortably, with good airflow.
travel.pets.domestic-road: Keep your {pet} contained and never leave it in a parked car
travel.pets.domestic-road.sub: A parked car can get dangerously hot or cold in minutes.
travel.pets.domestic-road.1: Animals that could distract the driver should be in a carrier or secured.
travel.pets.domestic-road.2: Don’t let pets ride loose in the back of a pickup truck.
travel.pets.domestic-road.3: On long trips, bring food and water and stop often so your {pet} can rest and walk.
travel.pets.cert.title: Start with your vet.
travel.pets.cert.body: As soon as you know your travel details, ask your veterinarian for help: requirements can include a health certificate, vaccinations, tests or medications, on set timelines.
travel.pets.us.title: Going to the U.S. with your dog?
travel.pets.us.body: Since August 1, 2024, the U.S. CDC has its own rules for dogs. A dog that was in a country at high risk for rabies in the past 6 months can’t enter the U.S. directly from Canada.
travel.pets.handoffInNote: Answer a few questions to see exactly what your animal needs.
travel.pets.handoffOutNote: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency’s guide to travelling with a pet, on inspection.canada.ca.
travel.pets.handoffHomeNote: Tips for trips by car and by plane, on travel.gc.ca.
ev.title: EV incentive
ev.subtitle: Electric Vehicle Affordability Program · Transport Canada

ev.error.body: The program page lists the incentive amounts, eligible vehicles and how to get it.
ev.handoffNote: You don’t apply yourself: an enrolled dealer checks eligibility and takes it off your bill.
ev.footnote: Individuals can get one incentive over the program. Provincial rebates are separate.
ev.hero.sub: For a new {fuel}, bought or leased for 48 months or more, in {year}.
ev.hero.subLease: Prorated for a {months}-month lease of a {fuel} (full amount {full} at 48 months).
ev.hero.no.price.sub: The final transaction value must be {cap} or less, unless the vehicle is made in Canada.
ev.hero.no.lease-short.sub: Only leases of 12 months or more get an incentive.
ev.hero.no.not-started.sub: Transactions started before that date don’t qualify, whatever the delivery date.
ev.hero.no.ended.sub: The program runs until March 31, 2031, or until the money runs out.
ev.calc.title: Your vehicle
ev.ca.sub: No price cap for Canadian-made EVs
ev.calc.note: The value counts the price, options, accessories, dealer fees and discounts. Taxes, freight and PDI, one set of winter tires, a Level 2 charger and registration fees don’t count.
ev.years.title: The incentive steps down
ev.years.note: The amount depends on when the dealer submits your eligibility check, not when you signed.
ev.funds.title: Money left in the program
ev.funds.note: {pct}% of the funding remains. Incentives are first come, first served until March 31, 2031.

ev.list.results: {count, plural, =0 {No matching models} one {# matching model} other {# matching models}}
ev.list.hint: Models on Transport Canada’s list of eligible vehicles. Tap one to use its type.
ev.list.none: Not on the list? It can still qualify if it meets the rules and its final transaction value is $50,000 or less.
ev.list.note: Being on the list doesn’t guarantee a purchase qualifies.

drone.verdict.young.basic.sub: Pilots under 14 can fly this drone only under the direct supervision of someone who holds a drone pilot certificate.
drone.verdict.young.advanced.sub: Pilots under 16 can fly an Advanced operation only under the direct supervision of someone with an Advanced or Level 1 Complex certificate.
drone.verdict.young.complex.sub: Under 18, Level 1 Complex flights are allowed only for training, directly supervised by a Level 1 Complex pilot who is 18 or older.
boat.limit.north: No youth limits in Nunavut or the NWT
boat.limit.over: This engine is over the limit: someone 16 or older must supervise.
travel.cannabis.over: Over the 30 g limit: carry less
travel.cannabis.over.sub: That’s more than an adult may carry in public, on a flight or on the road. Bring no more than 30 g of dried cannabis or its equivalent.
travel.calc.formHint: Edibles, topicals and drinks: up to 3% THC. Vapes, hash and concentrates: over 3% THC.
drone.handoff.portalNoteOwner: The owner (14 or older) registers the drone and pays the fee in Transport Canada’s Drone Management Portal.
drone.tcFeesOwner: to register, paid by the owner
drone.step.young-register-owner: An owner 14 or older registers the drone
drone.step.young-register-owner.detail: Usually a parent. It takes about 3 minutes online; mark the registration number on the drone.
drone.step.young-supervisor.basic: Find a certified pilot to supervise them
drone.step.young-supervisor.basic.detail: They must hold a Basic, Advanced or Level 1 Complex drone pilot certificate.
drone.step.young-supervisor.advanced: Find an Advanced pilot to supervise them
drone.step.young-supervisor.advanced.det: They must hold an Advanced or Level 1 Complex drone pilot certificate.
drone.step.young-supervisor.complex: Find a Level 1 Complex pilot to supervise them
drone.step.young-supervisor.complex.deta: They must hold a Level 1 Complex certificate and be 18 or older.
drone.step.young-fly.basic: They fly under that pilot’s direct supervision
drone.step.young-fly.basic.detail: Every flight, with the certified pilot directly supervising. They don’t need an exam or certificate for this.
drone.step.young-fly.advanced: They fly under that pilot’s direct supervision
drone.step.young-fly.advanced.detail: Every Advanced flight, with the certified pilot directly supervising.
drone.step.young-fly.complex: Training flights only, under that pilot’s supervision
drone.step.young-fly.complex.detail: Under 18, Level 1 Complex flights are allowed only for training.
drone.step.young-later.basic: At {min}, they take the Small Basic Exam
drone.step.young-later.basic.detail: Once they pass, they’re certified right away and can fly on their own.
drone.step.young-later.advanced: At {min}, they take the Advanced Exam
drone.step.young-later.advanced.detail: Then they pass a flight review and get their own Advanced certificate.
drone.step.young-later.complex: At {min}, they can start the Level 1 Complex path
drone.step.young-later.complex.detail: Ground school, the Level 1 Complex Exam and a flight review.
boat.lost.title: Your course provider can replace your card
boat.lost.sub: Only course providers accredited by Transport Canada can issue a replacement, and they charge a fee for it. Your card is valid for life.
boat.lost.1: Find the provider that issued it
boat.lost.1.body: Transport Canada’s Course Provider Lookup finds your course provider.
boat.lost.2.body: Only providers that are still accredited can issue one. Each sets its own fee; none of it goes to the government.
boat.lost.3: Carry the new card on board
boat.lost.3.body: A paper or electronic copy isn’t accepted: carry the card itself.
boat.lost.handoffNote: Transport Canada’s Course Provider Lookup. Your provider replaces the card, for a fee.
boat.limit.pwc: No personal watercraft under 16, even supervised
